uttarā.notes: DN 14:1.12.15 names Koṇāgamana’s birth mother. It gives no support for the entry’s additional identification as his chief female disciple. AN 8.91–117:1.1 lists both a bare Uttarā and Uttarā Nandamātā, so a single choice for the whole list would mislabel the first occurrence. AN 1.262 names Nanda’s mother in the compound uttarānandamātā. AN 8.89–90 are page overlaps. Thag 17.3 leaves the addressee unnamed. The identification with Uttarā 03 comes from commentary. The candidates omit the child in SN 10.7 and the elders of Thig 1.15 and 7.1 (DPPN’s Uttarā 7, 1 and 2 respectively). The packet also picks up masculine Uttara in AN 8.8, DN 23, MN 91 and MN 152, and a town name and a directional adjective in SN 42.13.

uttiya.notes: AN 10.95 calls its questioner a wanderer throughout. DPPN only conjectures that he became the elder of Thag 1.30. The elder’s two SN episodes concern the five kinds of sensual stimulation and a teaching in brief. SN 45.29, 45.31, 47.15 and 47.17 share their pages. The citation of Thag 1.51 begins the four companions’ rain verses with Godhika. Uttiya speaks at 1.54. The chapter recaps in SN 47.20, Thag 1.60 and Thag 1.100 point back to SN 47.16, Thag 1.54 and Thag 1.99 respectively. None of the candidates describes Mahinda’s companion.

uṇṇābha.notes: SN 48.42 is the brahmin’s conversation with the Buddha about the faculties. SN 48.41 shares the page. SN 51.15 records a brahmin of this name questioning Ānanda about abandoning desire. The entry leaves open whether the two speakers are the same man. SN 48.50 and 51.20 mention him in chapter recaps.

vacchagotta.notes: MN 73 follows the wanderer through ordination to arahantship and calls him tevijjo, as the elder calls himself in Thag 1.112. Thag 1.120:2.1 recaps his verse. AN 3.57 is the conversation about gifts in the Vacchagottasutta to which entry 01 refers (AN i 160). AN 3.63:2.1 calls the questioner about luxurious beds venāgapuriko vacchagotto brāhmaṇo. Entry 02 treats his identity with the wanderer as a possibility. Its MN and SN citations illustrate the first man’s travels. The Tevijja discourse is MN 71, numbered 72 in entry 01. AN 3.62, MN 70, SN 32.56–57 and SN 44.6 are page overlaps. The abbreviated SN 33 passages absent from the packet address him as Vaccha.

vajirā.notes: Vajirā answers Māra with the chariot simile in SN 5.10. The adjacent SN 5.8 and 5.9 feature Sīsupacālā and Selā. In MN 35:14.1 vajiraṁ is the iron thunderbolt held by Vajirapāṇī.

vajjiputta.notes: The sole candidate is a title entry for the Vajjiputta or Vesāli Sutta. It refers the reader to the separate biography of Vajjiputta (1). SN 9.9 calls the monk vajjiputtako and its verses about the log in the forest recur in Thag 1.62. Thag 1.119 attributes a different verse, addressed to Gotama, to the second elder. Both biographies are missing from the candidates. The chapter recaps name the elders at Thag 1.70:2.1 and 1.120:2.5. SN 9.7–8 share the cited page.

vajjiyamāhita.notes: AN 10.94:1.2 says he left Campā (campāya nikkhami). The English gives Sāvatthī, the setting of the preceding Anāthapiṇḍika discourse, AN 10.93. At the other citation the householder list reads vijayamāhiko (AN 6.120–139:1.16), translated as Vijayamāhita and indexed by DPD under vijayamāhika. AN 6.119 and 6.140 share the page.

vajjī.notes: AN 4.1 locates Bhaṇḍagāma in the country. AN 5.58 uses the same name for the people, whom the entry also covers. The itinerary is in SN 55.6. SN 55.5 shares the page. SN 35.87:13.5 calls Pubbajira a vajjigāmo in a compound. It places families friendly to Channa there without saying he was born there.

vakkali.notes: The ranking for faith is AN 1.208. The three cited AN groups start later. SN 22.87 describes the sick elder and Snp 5.19:16.1 names him as an example of faith. Thag 5.8 attributes the wind-ailment verses to him in the compound Vakkalitthero. SN 22.86 concerns Anurādha. Iti 92 is a thematic parallel about seeing the teaching and does not name Vakkali. Iti 93 shares the page.

valāhaka.notes: DN 17:1.13.2 names Mahāsudassana’s royal steed, and SN 22.96:4.6 names the horse ridden by the Buddha as a king in the past. Sujato translates Valāhaka as Thundercloud, so the packet misses both. MN 129:37.2 also says valāhako nāma assarājā of a wheel-turning monarch’s horse. Its wording gives an individual name. The claim about a family of horses in Valāhaka 01 rests on the commentarial material.

vappa.notes: AN 4.195 identifies the Sakyan follower of the Jains. AN 4.194 concerns the Koliyans at Sāpūga. Thag 1.61 attributes the verse to the elder and the chapter recap names him again at Thag 1.70:2.1, outside the packet. Neither entry concerns the month.

varadhara.notes: AN 4.30 and 4.185 both place him with Annabhāra and Sakuludāyī by the Sippinikā. The citation list misses AN 4.185 and picks up AN 4.28–29 beside AN 4.30.

varaṇā.notes: In the app, Mahākaccāna meets Ārāmadaṇḍa at Varaṇā in AN 2.37, one earlier than DPD’s example. The Pali has bhaddasāritīre where DPPN and the English name Kaddama Lake.

varuṇa.notes: DN 13 invokes the god and SN 11.3 calls him varuṇassa devarājassa in the passage about his banner. The hits in DN 20:13.3 and 15.5 are plural and belong to the group Varuṇā.

vassakāra.notes: DN 16:1.2.1 identifies Ajātasattu’s minister. Although the entry says the Dīgha account omits Sunidha, DN 16:1.26.1 explicitly names both builders of Pāṭaligāma as sunidhavassakārā. Ud 8.6:15.1 uses the same compound, which has its own DPD line.

vatrabhū.notes: In SN 2.3:3.4 the Buddha addresses the godling Māgha by this epithet. SN 2.4 and 2.5 share the cited page and address different godlings.

vaḍḍha.notes: Thag 5.5 credits his mother’s advice and contains five verses (335–339). The entry counts six. His mother addresses Vaḍḍha directly in Thig 9.1, including at 3.4, where the English omits the vocative and the packet misses it.
